newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers with rupiah, but seen weaker.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers with rupiah, but seen weaker.

text.p: The ringgit followed dollar/rupiah for most of the day, making a slight recovery along with the Indonesian unit in the later half, dealers said on Tuesday.
The ringgit declined to a low of 2.8050 to a dollar in the morning, when rupiah fell below 3,000 per dollar level, before recovering to 2.7850/9030 at the close of Kuala Lumpur market.
Thin volumes continued to exaggerate movements with initial fall of the ringgit slowed by dollar sales from Kuala Lumpur exporters, they said.
The dealers predicted a further decline for the Malaysian unit in the near-term.
"The market is now targetting dollar/ringgit going up to 2.90," a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
But other dealers said the ringgit would consolidate in the 2.75-2.80 range in the near-term.
"Unless either side breaks convincingly, we should see very rangey sort of play for a while," a dealer with another European bank in Singapore said.
"But, the mood is still for a weaker ringgit and stronger dollar," he added.
